## Purpose

Part of #12131.

xgrammar 0.2.7, pinned in #57272, includes mlc-ai/xgrammar#836: the `additionalProperties` value schema is now honored when `propertyNames` is also present (it fixes mlc-ai/xgrammar#826). `has_xgrammar_unsupported_json_features` still treats that combination as unsupported, so schemas like the one below needlessly skip the xgrammar backend:

```json
{"type": "object", "propertyNames": {"pattern": "^[a-z_]+$"}, "additionalProperties": {"type": "integer"}}
```

This PR removes the `additionalProperties` condition from the `propertyNames` fallback. The `properties`, `patternProperties` and `unevaluatedProperties` conditions stay, because they are still not enforced in 0.2.7 (I checked each against the compiled grammar).

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR touches this condition. #56557, #56753 and #48416 change other parts of the same function. For the integer `multipleOf` gap, which 0.2.7 also closes, I left a note on #48416 because that PR rewrites that line.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests below.

**Additional changes from @arpera**:
For each unsupported by xgrammar schema case I added a bug tracking issue report on xgrammar to allow us more easily track bug fixes in xgrammar and react more swiftly on such things.
All my changes are equivalent to main branch, verified this by both: agent and also run all the unit tests from `tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_xgrammar.py`.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/structured_output/test_utils.py tests/v1/structured_output/test_validation.py -v
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_xgrammar.py tests/v1/structured_output/test_utils.py
```

- Moved the schema from `unsupported_property_names_combinations` to the supported list.
- Added `test_property_names_keeps_additional_properties_value_schema`. It asserts that the compiled grammar accepts `{"score": 5}` and rejects both a bad key (`{"Score": 5}`) and a bad value (`{"score": "seven"}`).

## Test Result

- Before the fix: `test_supported_json_features[property_names_with_additional_properties_schema]` fails. The new grammar test already passes on xgrammar 0.2.7, which confirms the upstream fix.
- After the fix: 70 passed. ruff, mypy and the other pre-commit hooks pass.

Model evals are not needed: the change only affects which backend is chosen for this schema shape, and the grammar test covers the output constraint directly.

detail.body:
## Purpose

Part of #12131.

xgrammar 0.2.7, pinned in #57272, includes mlc-ai/xgrammar#836: the `additionalProperties` value schema is now honored when `propertyNames` is also present (it fixes mlc-ai/xgrammar#826). `has_xgrammar_unsupported_json_features` still treats that combination as unsupported, so schemas like the one below needlessly skip the xgrammar backend:

```json
{"type": "object", "propertyNames": {"pattern": "^[a-z_]+$"}, "additionalProperties": {"type": "integer"}}
```

This PR removes the `additionalProperties` condition from the `propertyNames` fallback. The `properties`, `patternProperties` and `unevaluatedProperties` conditions stay, because they are still not enforced in 0.2.7 (I checked each against the compiled grammar).

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR touches this condition. #56557, #56753 and #48416 change other parts of the same function. For the integer `multipleOf` gap, which 0.2.7 also closes, I left a note on #48416 because that PR rewrites that line.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests below.

**Additional changes from @arpera**:
For each unsupported by xgrammar schema case I added a bug tracking issue report on xgrammar to allow us more easily track bug fixes in xgrammar and react more swiftly on such things.
All my changes are equivalent to main branch, verified this by both: agent and also run all the unit tests from `tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_xgrammar.py`.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/structured_output/test_utils.py tests/v1/structured_output/test_validation.py -v
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_xgrammar.py tests/v1/structured_output/test_utils.py
```

- Moved the schema from `unsupported_property_names_combinations` to the supported list.
- Added `test_property_names_keeps_additional_properties_value_schema`. It asserts that the compiled grammar accepts `{"score": 5}` and rejects both a bad key (`{"Score": 5}`) and a bad value (`{"score": "seven"}`).

## Test Result

- Before the fix: `test_supported_json_features[property_names_with_additional_properties_schema]` fails. The new grammar test already passes on xgrammar 0.2.7, which confirms the upstream fix.
- After the fix: 70 passed. ruff, mypy and the other pre-commit hooks pass.

Model evals are not needed: the change only affects which backend is chosen for this schema shape, and the grammar test covers the output constraint directly.

+            "properties": {"Bad": {"type": "integer"}},

+        #
+        # ========================================================
+        # propertyNames + unevaluatedProperties is unsupported by xgrammar
+        # Tracking issue: https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar/issues/961
+        #

         # value type, so it drops unevaluatedProperties whether it restricts
         # values (a schema) or forbids them (false).
         {
             "type": "object",
             "propertyNames": {"pattern": "^[a-z]+$"},
-            "unevaluatedProperties": {"type": "integer"},

         schema_types = _schema_types(obj)
 
-        # Check for numeric ranges
+        # integer/number + multipleOf is unsupported by xgrammar
+        # This is known behavior and xgrammar emits warning in logs:
+        #   [21:18:08] /project/cpp/json_schema_converter.cc:1053:

+        # This warning was added in PR
+        # https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar/pull/670
+        # So, no need to track progress on this
         if (schema_types & {"integer", "number"}) and ("multipleOf" in obj):
             return True
 
-        # Check for array unsupported keywords
+        # array + some constraints is unsupported by xgrammar
+        # Tracking issue: https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar/issues/968
         if "array" in schema_types and any(
             key in obj
             for key in ("uniqueItems", "contains", "minContains", "maxContains")
         ):
             return True
 
-        # Unsupported keywords for strings
+        # string + format with unsupported keywords
+        # is unsupported by xgrammar
+        # Tracking issue: https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar/issues/967
+        # See tests on this in test_backend_xgrammar.py
+        # unsupported_string_schemas
         if (
             "string" in schema_types
             and "format" in obj
             and obj["format"] not in STRING_SUPPORTED_FORMATS
         ):
             return True
 
-        # A string mixing a generative constraint (pattern or format) with
-        # explicit length bounds. xgrammar compiles the pattern/format side
-        # and silently drops minLength/maxLength from the grammar, so output

-        # to {0, N} correctly.
+        # string + format/pattern + length constraint is unsupported by xgrammar

+        # unsupported_string_schemas

-        # propertyNames validates names, so it is a string schema even when it

-        if (

-            and "propertyNames" in obj

-            return True
-

-        # properties, conflict under xgrammar.

-            "object" in schema_types
-            and isinstance(obj.get("patternProperties"), dict)
-            and ("properties" in obj or len(obj["patternProperties"]) > 1)
-        ):
-            return True

+        # unsupported_propertyNames_combinations

+            # propertyNames + maxLength is unsupported by xgrammar
+            # Tracking issue: https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar/issues/960
+            property_names = obj.get("propertyNames")
+            if isinstance(property_names, dict) and _has_pattern_and_length_bounds(
+                property_names
+            ):
+                return True
+            # propertyNames + patternProperties is unsupported by xgrammar
+            # Tracking issue: https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar/issues/959
+            if "patternProperties" in obj:
+                return True
+            # propertyNames + properties is unsupported by xgrammar
+            # Tracking issue: https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar/issues/958
+            if "properties" in obj:
+                return True
+            # propertyNames + unevaluatedProperties is unsupported by xgrammar
+            # Tracking issue: https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar/issues/961
+            if obj.get("unevaluatedProperties", True) is not True:
+                return True
+
+        # patternProperties is not supported in pair with some constraints
+        # in xgrammar
+        # See tests on this in test_backend_xgrammar.py
+        # unsupported_patternProperties_combinations
+        if "object" in schema_types and isinstance(obj.get("patternProperties"), dict):
+            # patternProperties + properties is unsupported by xgrammar
+            # Tracking issue: https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar/issues/964
+            if "properties" in obj:
+                return True
+            # patternProperties + patternProperties is unsupported by xgrammar
+            # Tracking issue: https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar/issues/965
+            if len(obj["patternProperties"]) > 1:
+                return True
 
         # Note(arpera):
         # Xgrammar lacks support of multi-branch allOf
@@ -370,8 +384,7 @@ def check_object(obj: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
         # would accept any kind of json, such as
         # "maybe", "", 42, {}, [], {"a": 1}, etc.
         # which is NOT what is expected.
-        # Reported this issue to xgrammar team to track progress on resolving:
-        # https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar/issues/937
+        # Tracking issue: https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar/issues/937
         allof = obj.get("allOf")
         if isinstance(allof, list) and len(allof) >= 2:
             return True
